parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal/national passport, visa and entry rules are traveler-facing; document doubt or mismatch can trigger refusal, additional screening, or a permanent fraud bar, and airport/federal facilities remain restricted. The state/province adds equality, public-accommodation, hate-crime, identity-document and shield-law protections, plus inclusive school rulings, which should reduce local service, hotel, clinic and minor-care friction. But state enforcement against federal border screening, custody or facilities is not documented. Federal custody conversion-therapy, hormone denial and immigration-custody abuse are severe. For minors, state shield/education protections help, while federal care criminalisation, sports pressure and detention links create unresolved risk. Upper high-risk band, just below elevated.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require M/F assigned birth, block new X markers and visas where records cast doubt on sex; reports include confiscated or blocked passports, stranded travellers, refusal, and possible permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: State offers X ID/birth certificates, legal-aid FAQ, ongoing litigation, and existing X passports remain valid until expiry. State IDs cannot cure national passport or visa mismatch.
entry_documents.interaction: Border and visa screening precede state protections; document discrepancy can escalate into investigation, refusal, or lifetime immigration bar.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopt trans-inmate conversion therapy, hair cuts, hormone removal and care denial; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. State custody practice and minor family placement not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law and state bias-crime enhancements exist; state anti-discrimination law. No documented state pre-emption of federal custody practices.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A police or immigration encounter can move a traveller into federal custody, where state shield law does not stop placement, care denial or abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, removes pronoun/naming policies, and airport guidance warns invasive screening/outting. No state-specific facility ban documented here.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation and public-services equality law covers gender identity; religious employers exempt. Enforcement not documented and cannot override national facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State may protect private/state facilities, but national-owned/funded settings and federal screening remain restricted; appearance or documents can trigger checks.

care_services.exposure: National policies criminalise minors’ gender-affirming care, investigate schools, freeze funding, subpoena records, and deny hormones in custody. Adult visitor medication or refill friction is not documented.
care_services.protection: State shield protects patients/providers for care legal here when home jurisdiction banned; state services/education anti-discrimination and school coverage exist. Shield categories and enforcement uncertain.
care_services.interaction: State shielding can operate for care visits, but detention or federal facilities override it; minors/guardians face national school-care pressure alongside state refuge.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders and counterterrorism text frame gender ideology or radically pro-transgender groups as extremist; Do Not Travel flags and visa advisories exist. No national presentation crime, but fraud/facility enforcement does.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment/hate-crime protections, state equality law, panic-defence repeal, and inclusive school rulings exist. Enforcement statistics absent; national investigations target state institutions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing increases border, police and federal custody exposure; state law may mitigate local service encounters but not national enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans/nonbinary minors face same entry screening and national care/school criminalisation; family or immigration custody severe, though placement/separation not documented. Guardians risk linked visa, fraud and detention exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-discrimination in education, inclusive school policy, shield law for legal care, X IDs and partner recognition may support families. Operational effect not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: State refuge can help minors seeking care or school access, but federal border, custody, sports investigations and funding pressure can reach the whole family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented: state-specific street violence, police extortion or targeted raids against trans travellers. Federal screening, counterterrorism framing and custody reports raise reporting/chill risks.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancements and panic-defence repeal; national hate-crime law; no organised local targeting record found. Charging and prosecution data absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If violence occurs, police interaction may expose documents and escalate toward federal custody; no evidence of reliable protection for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Not documented: state enforcement of public-accommodation/shield law, family/minor detention, marker-change effects at border, discipline for federal screening, or state override of national facilities.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, legal-aid FAQ, state equality law and court precedents exist. No documented orders or inspections change federal border/custody/facility practice for travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation creates timing-dependent exposure; protective state law may reduce friction but does not prove pre-emption or effective enforcement.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has birth-sex rules for all public buildings and rejected complaints, similar to the national facility and screening exposure here. This jurisdiction is more dangerous through visa fraud bars and federal custody abuse, but better through state public-accommodation, hate-crime and shield protections, so it sits near, slightly above, 0.35-A.

0.25-C has a national presentation offence plus local passport confiscation and extortion. Here, no general presentation crime exists and state protections are substantial, making it above 0.25-C. But severe federal visa screening, federal facilities restrictions and immigration-custody abuse still keep it below the elevated-risk tier.

0.55-B has local service hostility but functioning inspectors, prosecutions and no universal birth-sex facility rule. The state-side law here resembles that profile, yet the combined regime includes unresolved federal entry, facility and custody exposures that state law does not cancel, so it is clearly below 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is dominated by federal border, visa, facility and custody restrictions, while state/provincial equality, shield and education laws materially reduce local service and care friction. Because no documented state enforcement or pre-emption changes federal screening, national facilities, or immigration/federal custody, the final operative journey remains high risk. For minors, state shield and school protections are meaningful but unstable under national care criminalisation, investigations and detention exposure; unresolved custody, enforcement and family-placement details increase uncertainty without reducing risk.
